初看卡片效果纷繁多样，最核心的有几点：
1. 主动使用行动效果相当于亏影响力点数，除非确实有意义能带来局面变化，否则不要主动使用。
2. 对你负面的对手行动，即使暂时规避了，洗牌之后也会再回来，如果到对手手里在一个关键的时刻使用更糟糕。选择一个恰当的时机提前触发掉比较好。
基于以上两点建立了一种需要斟酌平衡的策略机制。
3. 除了那些明显有强大效果的行动，关注那些不会被移除的牌。这些牌在中后期会被反复触发，带来的影响比初看上去的要更大。

Дисклеймер: рецензия написана исходя из того, что вы представляете себе игру в настольном варианте. Если нет — это глобальная стратегия дуэльного формата, основанная на механике контроля территорий и довольно типичная для GMT Games... короче, почитайте Тесеру или BoardGameGeek, это одна из известнейших настольных игр в целом. В рецензии подробный пересказ будет лишним, просто знайте, что исходная настольная версия заслуживает 10 из 10.

До выхода этой игры — официальной цифровой версии Twilight Struggle — единственной вменяемой альтернативой посиделкам за живым столом был VASSAL. Это рабочий, но сложный инструмент, требующий настройки и терпения. ПК-версия Twilight Struggle выигрывает у него в первую очередь удобством и доступностью. Весь процесс организации матча сведён к минимуму: купили игру, привязали учётную запись к электронной почте — и можно искать соперника. Никаких сторонних клиентов или долгих настроек модулей, всё работает из коробки.

Визуально игра практически дословно цитирует настольный первоисточник. Дизайн перенесён бережно, а интерфейс хоть и не вызывает восторга своей изобретательностью, со своей задачей справляется. К UI/UX можно придраться в мелочах — всегда есть ощущение, что какие-то элементы можно было расположить удобнее, — но это тот случай, когда интерфейс не мешает процессу. Вы не боретесь с управлением, а играете. Но если вы плохо знаете английский и не слишком близко знакомы с настольным первоисточником — имейте в виду, что тут нет русской локализации.

Однако если рассматривать Twilight Struggle как одиночную игру, восторг быстро улетучивается, потому что её сильно портит искусственный интеллект. Для новичка он может показаться компетентным, но если у вас за плечами есть хотя бы полсотни партий с живыми людьми, компьютер перестаёт быть соперником. Он играет шаблонно, используя очень ограниченный набор стратегий, и совершенно не чувствует мету. Бесполезно ждать, что он хитрым образом заставит вас разыграть CIA Created или Lone Gunman при DEFCON 2 — он не понимает таких тонкостей, зато вполне может случайно проиграть сам, загнав себя в такую же ситуацию.

ИИ не только слабый, но и медленный. Наблюдать за тем, как компьютер полминуты обдумывает довольно очевидный ход, утомительно — а это происходит регулярно, десятки раз за партию. В итоге игра с компьютером теряет динамику окончательно.

Цифровая версия Twilight Struggle — отличный инструмент для игры с друзьями, которые живут в других городах, и самая удобная платформа для сетевых баталий против рандомов из лобби. Но как самостоятельная игра против компьютера она быстро выдыхается: тренироваться на таком ИИ быстро надоедает, а удовольствие от победы над ним исчезает, как только вы понимаете его логику.

7 из 10

Disclaimer: This review assumes you are familiar with the tabletop version. If not, just know that it is a two-player grand strategy game based on area control mechanics — classic GMT Games fare. I won't rehash the rules here; check BoardGameGeek for that. Suffice it to say, the original board game is a solid 10/10 masterpiece.

Before this official digital adaptation dropped, the only sane alternative to gathering around a physical table was VASSAL. While functional, VASSAL is a complex tool requiring setup and patience. The PC version of Twilight Struggle beats it hands down purely on convenience and accessibility. The process of setting up a match is streamlined to the max: buy the game, link your account to an email, and you’re ready to find an opponent. No third-party clients or tedious module configurations — it just works right out of the box.

Visually, the game is practically a carbon copy of the tabletop source material. The design has been transferred with care, and while the interface won’t win any awards for innovation, it gets the job done. You could nitpick the UI/UX — there’s always a nagging feeling that certain elements could have been positioned better — but ultimately, the interface doesn’t get in the way. You’re playing the game, not fighting the controls.

However, if you treat Twilight Struggle as a single-player experience, the excitement evaporates quickly because the Artificial Intelligence severely drags it down. It might seem competent to a rookie, but if you have even fifty games against humans under your belt, the computer ceases to be a challenge. It plays robotically, relying on a very limited set of strategies, and has absolutely no grasp of the meta. Don’t expect it to cleverly trick you into playing "CIA Created" or "Lone Gunman" at DEFCON 2 — it doesn't understand those nuances. In fact, it’s just as likely to accidentally lose the game by backing itself into that exact corner.

The AI isn't just weak; it’s slow. Watching the computer spend thirty seconds "thinking" about a painfully obvious move is exhausting — and this happens dozens of times per match. As a result, playing against the CPU completely kills the game's pacing.

The digital version of Twilight Struggle is an excellent tool for playing with friends in different cities and is easily the most convenient platform for online battles against random opponents. But as a standalone single-player PC game, it runs out of steam (pun intended) fast. Practicing against this AI gets boring, and the satisfaction of winning vanishes the moment you figure out its logic.

7/10

Twilight Struggle is an absolute gem for anyone who loves strategy games with historical depth and immersive atmosphere. This digital adaptation of the classic board game brilliantly captures the tension and paranoia of the Cold War, putting you in the shoes of either the USA or USSR as you vie for global influence.
The game’s historical depth is its shining star. Every card is steeped in real-world events, from the Cuban Missile Crisis to the Space Race, making each playthrough feel like a gripping history lesson. The mechanics are tight, balancing strategy and luck in a way that keeps you on edge without feeling unfair. The atmosphere—enhanced by the art, music, and flavor text—perfectly evokes the high-stakes drama of the era.
Sure, the game is a bit older, and the visuals might not be cutting-edge, but that doesn’t detract from its brilliance. The depth of strategy and replayability make it timeless. Whether you’re a history buff or just love intense, thoughtful gameplay, Twilight Struggle is a must-play. Highly recommended!

[*] [b]Strike 1[/b] was the unimpressive AI that gleefully prioritizes "Indo-Pakistani War" but ignores other targets of opportunity in their deck, or overpays for influence in controlled countries because it knows the scoring card for the continent is in the player's hand. Even by cheating and with full information, the intelligence of the computer is comically inept and not competitive in Single Player

[*] [b]Strike 2[/b] was the clear edge in dice rolls vs. the CPU, presumably as a workaround due to weak AI. This has been described elsewhere so there is no doubt that the number of 1's and 6's rolled is impossible and would never occur in a random number generator. In Single Player mode, the stupid AI player is clearly given an edge to improve it's poor talent for strategy.

[*] [b]Strike 3[/b] is the many bugged achievements for "Twilight Struggle" that will later leave this title forever incomplete in my library, sticking out like a missing book on a shelf. It is currently impossible to complete about half of them, which you can confirm by viewing the global achievements.

While "Twilight Struggle" is one of the most well-regarded board games available, this PC adaptation is depressingly weak and unworthy of being sold as a Single-Player title. The AI is clearly following a kind-of tiered strategy and can be easily manipulated once you learn the patterns - for example, it will always coup available non-battleground countries with foreign influence meaning that you could profitably waste the AI's time by blanketing Africa with influence from [u]Decolonization[/u]/[u]Colonial Rear Guards[/u] and watch it coup away for 4 turns while the player pursues important business.

This title is not a total loss though - it still enables a decent multiplayer game. The UI has been controversial in other reviews, but I think it's crisp and informative and I like the way the cards move across the screen. The matchmaking is satisfactory and the rules aren't bent when playing with humans, so that offers some redemption to this compact title. In truth, the title really comes into it's own when solely used as a multiplayer matchmaker.

But I'm not in any mood to forgive the clear, obvious, unmistakable, transparent bugginess of the achievements. It's plain from statistics that no players are successfully earning them, and still the devs considered this fine and moved off to another project without fixing an issue that can be seen right on the storefront. I am aware that not everyone cares, but I do and I'm planting a flag here that I don't accept it happily and don't think anyone else should either.

In the niche case that you (1) like "Twilight Struggle" and (2) mainly play multiplayer and (3) don't care about achievements, then this title is probably fine and worth the money that you're paying if purchased on sale. It really reminds me of the old AOL Channels that offered board games that could be played with participants around the world, so it's a small hit of nostalgia that I enjoyed while it lasted. But if you want to pick up "TS" every so often between breaks or can't commit to long MP matches, then this release really won't satisfy that void.
